name: aquarium_landen_75 keep-out for viscous_waterproof_01
purpose: Workspace box that gates every joint target sent to the real arm in the tank (makermodslab/tank_guard.py). Gavin 2026-11-07: "can we now build a bounding box to run dream1?" and "the floor of the aquarium is the only part of the aquarium the arm is allowed to touch anyways".
units: mm, motor degrees (after the full-turn unwrap)

yaw_deg.source: New base mount (2026-11-13): yaw now rests on Gavin squaring the truss post flush on the back glass between his marker lines; not traced on this mount, and the weak clamp lets the base rotate if pushed. Old loose base: trace 20261108T044404Z (evidence copy in configs/viscous/viscous_waterproof_01/evidence/tank-trace-20261108T044404Z.jsonl): +y wall line through every-vertex extremes has 0.25 deg of yaw over 224 mm of travel; the earlier probe fit read about 1 deg. Taken as 0; a residual yaw of 1 deg moves the wall at most ~10 mm at full reach, inside the 30 mm margin.

left.source: New base mount, CAD from Gavin's 3MF (2026-11-13): J1 sits 50 mm from the +y edge of the 80 mm wide truss post, and Gavin resets the post to the middle of the back glass on marker lines before each run, so the gap to the +y glass is (434 inner width - 80) / 2 = 177 mm and the wall is 50 + 177 = 227. Assumes the post centred on its marks; not traced on the new mount. Was 210, hand-traced 2026-11-07 on the old loose base (sd 1.7 mm over 237 mm).

right.source: New base mount, CAD (2026-11-13): J1 sits 30 mm from the post's -y edge, with the post centred on Gavin's marks the -y gap is 177 mm, so the wall is -(30 + 177) = -207. 227 + 207 = 434 mm = nominal inner width for 8 mm glass (the old trace's 210 + 224 agreed). Was -224, traced 2026-11-07 on the old loose base. This wall is 17 mm closer than before.

near.source: New base mount, CAD from Gavin's 3MF (2026-11-13): an upright L-bracket whose 12 mm vertical truss post stands flush against the back glass (Gavin confirmed flush); the arm bolts to its floor plate with J1 at the bolt pattern's centre. J1 to the post's inner face is 106 mm, to the glass 118 mm. The plane is the post face, the nearest thing behind J1; the 12 mm to the glass is left as slack for J1 sitting off the bolt centre. Not traced. Was 80 (Gavin 2026-11-08: "lets say the back wall is 8cm from the center of j1"); tank.json and the sim scene still use 40.

far.source: The back glass at 118 (mount CAD, 2026-11-13) minus the nominal inner length 734 mm. Taken from the glass, not from the 106 post face: near - 734 would put the far glass 12 mm too far away. The mount moved J1 38 mm further from the back glass than the 80 mm figure, so the far glass is now only a little beyond the arm's furthest collision point (~610 mm) and the far rule can bind at full reach. Was -654 (80 - 734).

floor.source: Live run 2026-11-08T213138Z: the gripper tip's lowest mesh point plateaued at -27.3..-28.3 mm for the last ~4 s while commands kept asking lower, i.e. the jaws resting on the floor glass (Gavin saw them touch and pressed STOP). Gavin: "Floor line from -31 to -28 mm" is fine. Was -31 (the arm lying at rest after the base was raised; the model reads a few mm low there).

rim.source: Lowest plausible rim: the floor at -28 mm plus the nominal 442 mm inner height (450 outer - 8 glass).

margins_mm.source: Gavin aquarium follow-up 2026-11-07: 30 mm moving-link wall/rim margin (tank.json surface_margins_mm). Covers FK error, tracking lag and the residual yaw; it does NOT cover the loose base sliding (~30 mm under a hand push), which must be clamped.

floor_press_mm.source: Floor is the one allowed contact surface (Gavin 2026-11-07). A target may put a vertex at most this far below the floor bound, so a command can never ask for a deep push into the floor glass. Padding does not apply to the floor. Was 10; raised to 20 on 2026-11-14 after the start gate refused the arm lying on the glass at its rest (wrist_yaw_link mesh 13.7 mm under the -28 line with J5 at +24 deg, i.e. the FK floor error varies by pose by more than 10 mm). Gavin: the pose was fine, the check "too strict". Dream's own floor slide target (floor + 10 mm + sag) is unchanged; only the guard's backstop depth moved.

padding_mm.source: Gavin: "there are a lot of cabling sticking out of the side of the arms, and not represented in the urdf". tank_geometry's unmeasured-link default of 40 mm; the fingers carry no cables and are the measured probe, so they use the mesh itself. Replace with measured cable padding (the tank-measure envelope touches) when available.

yaw_link.why: Rides on the base and turns with J1 only: its extent behind J1 is 30-42.5 mm at every J1 angle (never further), so it cannot approach a wall it does not already touch. It is part of the base footprint, like the base itself.

upper_arm_link.why: Its heel (around the J2 axis) sits 28 mm behind J1 whenever J2 <= -100 deg and reached 36.9 mm in the trace, so the full 70 mm near rule would refuse the arm's own rest. The heel stays limited to 40 mm behind J1, as it has been since the 40 mm estimate: with the near plane at the new mount's post face (106, 2026-11-13) that is a 66 mm margin and no padding. The heel is kept where it was, not given the post's extra 26 mm, because the new mount has a corner fin 42-50 mm to +y of J1 running from about 16 mm behind J1 back to the post, which the keep-out does not model; the shoulder came within 11-17 mm of it in logged poses, so the heel must not gain room toward it. Links beyond the elbow (J3, the hazard Gavin named) keep the full near margin and padding.

joint_limits_deg.source: configs/viscous/viscous_waterproof_01/evidence/lab-hardware-profile.json follower joint_limits. Note the arm rests at J1 182-191 in the tank, so a start at J1 > 187.53 is refused until it is moved inside by hand.

start_limit_tolerance_deg.source: The arm rests in the tank outside three soft limits (trace: J1 191 vs 187.5, J2 -201.7 vs -199.4, gripper -0.5 vs -2.9). A start this far outside is accepted, as the Lab's slow mode already does; the first target is clipped into the limits along a checked path.

max_jump_deg.source: Any arm joint target more than this from the last accepted target is refused outright, never slid toward: it catches a J1 wrap (+182 -> -178) and IK branch flips. At 20 Hz a 30 deg/s joint moves 1.5 deg per row.

sweep_tolerance_mm.source: Path check resolution: segments are sampled finely enough that no point of any link can move more than this between samples, and every sample must clear by this much, so the whole straight joint-space path is proven clear.

tracking_allowance_mm.source: The MEASURED pose may lag or sag from the target. A measured pose that eats more than this into the margin means the arm is not where the guard thinks: stop the run.
